name: The Inn at Perry Cabin
positioning: Historic waterfront inn on the Miles River in St. Michaels, Maryland, with its own sailing fleet, golf course and spa
best_for: Couples who want a waterfront Chesapeake Bay escape with sailing and golf
Travelers who like history and want to walk into a small harbor town

facts.text: The resort sits along the Miles River in the heart of St. Michaels, Maryland.
The historic waterfront retreat has roots dating back to the years following the War of 1812.
Samuel Hambleton designed the Morning Room after Commodore Perry's cabin on his flagship, which gave the inn its name.
Rooms were designed by Alexandra Champalimaud, combining modern furnishings with nautical decor.
Each room has a waterfront view or a view of the property's garden.
French doors open to private decks, patios and verandas.
The resort has a zero-edge pool and manicured gardens.
Complimentary bicycles, kayaks and paddleboards are available for exploring St. Michaels by land or water.
The property is a short walk from downtown St. Michaels.
The Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum is a direct neighbor of the Inn.
The skipjack Stanley Norman dates from 1902 and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
Dogs are welcome, and guests with pets get a first-floor room with direct outdoor access.

highlights.text: The fleet includes the historic 63-foot skipjack Stanley Norman.
The resort's fleet includes five sailboats and a 55-foot Hinckley yacht.
The resort has Links at Perry Cabin, a Pete Dye-designed golf course.
The Spa at Perry Cabin offers plant-based treatments made from herbs and aromatics grown in the Inn's own gardens or on Eastern Shore farms.

considerations.text: Baltimore-Washington International Airport is a 90-minute drive away, and driving from Washington or Baltimore crosses the Chesapeake Bay Bridge, which requires a toll.
Once Memorial Day arrives, St. Michaels is awash with visitors.
The layout of the property can get a bit confusing, though guests receive a map of the grounds.
